question: many labs run the same reference perturbation; does it look the same in every lab?

settings.features: e8: the columns fd.load_poscon() keeps, z-scored on the field's DMSO wells
settings.effect: one well minus the mean of its own plate's DMSO wells
settings.noise: one DMSO well minus the mean of its plate's other DMSO wells
settings.pairs: cosine between two single-well effects, never two wells of one plate
settings.labs_weighted: equally: own lab and other labs are means over labs, not over pairs

non_finite_values.handling: set to the plate's DMSO mean (no effect on that feature)

e8_field.what: plate-level effects (mean of about four wells of each control on a plate), every plate of every lab; e8-redteam compares a plate with the mean of its own lab (which includes the plate) and with the mean of the other labs; e8-same-drug gives mean cosine between pairs of plates

same_dose_only.note: labs at 10 uM only: source_7 (0.625 uM) left out

untreated_on_each_plate.what: each RSL3 well minus the mean of its own plate's DMSO wells; cells left as a share of the same wells

source_7.reason: source_7 assayed library compounds, RSL3 among them, at 0.625 uM; the other labs used 10 uM, 16 times more [7]. Side by side, a difference in dose would look like a difference between labs. Its positive controls were 5 uM, as in every lab.

dose_check.what: share of cells left after RSL3, against the same plate's DMSO wells, beside each lab's dose; descriptive only: one dose per lab, so dose and lab cannot be told apart for the lab at the lower dose

strongest_control_at_5_um.how_chosen: of the controls on the plates of every lab, the one that left the fewest cells, mean over labs

dose_check.controls_note: the eight positive controls were 5 uM in every lab, so their cells left are a same-dose reference for each lab's cells

images.window: percentiles 1 and 99.7 of the DMSO well's image, per lab and channel

caveats: RSL3 is one well on each of 12 plates: 5 in source_7, 4 in source_9, 2 in source_5, 1 in source_11. Own-lab agreement rests on 10, 6 and 1 pairs of wells, and does not exist for source_11.
Erastin is one well on each of 11 plates in six labs; only source_7 (5) and source_3 (2) have an own-lab value.

In source_5 and source_7 every RSL3 well sits at one plate position on plates of one layout, so own-lab agreement can include a shared layout effect; the same-position DMSO pairs there are small (about 0.06 to 0.07). source_9 puts its four RSL3 wells at four positions, and its same-position DMSO pairs agree at about 0.36: position matters more there.
source_7 ran its five RSL3 plates in five consecutive runs of one layout, and source_9 its four on one day: own-lab agreement there is agreement between repeats, close in time.
source_9 uses 1536-well plates, with fewer cells per well, so its single wells are noisier for every compound.
Single wells are noisier than e8's plate means; compare RSL3 with the controls on the same plates, not with e8's field numbers directly.

The dose is JUMP's, not chosen for ferroptosis, and it is not the same everywhere: source_7 assayed library compounds at 0.625 uM, every other site at 10 uM, while the positive controls were 5 uM at every site [7]. RSL3 left 75 to 87% of cells on all five source_7 plates, consistent with the 16-fold lower dose, while source_7's positive controls worked; dose and lab cannot be separated there. Erastin was weak in source_7 and also in source_15 at 10 uM. The per-well metadata does not record the dose.

Specificity: across labs RSL3 is only a little more like RSL3 than like some other compounds (NVS-PAK1-1, erastin); dying cells look alike. The result is an example of the question, not a ferroptosis fingerprint.
Cell counts are the repository's per-image estimate from the mean nuclei object index (field.COUNT), not a direct count.
